read.sections.1.text.note: Kept 'Great Green Wall' in brackets after 'Tembok Hijau Raksasa'; kept 'Djibouti' (KBBI spelling is 'Jibuti'). 'Fields' = 'lahan pertanian'. Mangrove = 'bakau'.
read.sections.1.text.back: All over the world, communities adapt to changes in their environment. In Bangladesh, many farm fields are underwater for months in the rainy season. Some farmers make floating gardens from water plants, then grow vegetables on them. In Africa, countries from Senegal to Djibouti are building the Great Green Wall (Great Green Wall). They plant trees and care for the soil so the land does not turn into desert. On many coasts in Asia, people plant mangrove trees, whose roots help protect the coast from waves. Each is a response that fits its place.
read.sections.1.text.source: Around the world, communities adapt to changes in their environment. In Bangladesh, many fields stay under water for months in the rainy season. Some farmers build floating gardens from water plants and grow vegetables on top. In Africa, countries from Senegal to Djibouti are working on the Great Green Wall. They plant trees and care for the land to stop it from turning into desert. On many coasts in Asia, people plant mangrove trees, whose roots help protect the shore from waves. Each of these is a response that fits the local place.

read.sections.2.text.note: 'phone or data' = 'ponsel atau kuota internet' (the everyday Indonesian way to say mobile data). Printed notices = 'pengumuman tercetak'; simpler uses 'pengumuman di kertas'.
read.sections.2.text.back: A response only works if people can use it. Look at the three ideas for Brookside. A warning sign is quick to make, but it does not make the bridge safer, and some people cannot read it. Raising the bridge reduces the risk, and the ramp helps people who use wheelchairs or push carts. Phone warnings can tell people earlier, but not everyone has a phone or internet data. Printed notices at the market can reach more people. Making sure everyone can use a plan is called inclusion. Often, two ideas used together work better than one, and it is useful to ask the people who use the bridge.
read.sections.2.text.source: A response only works if people can use it. Look at the three ideas for Brookside. A warning sign is quick, but it does not make the bridge safer, and some people cannot read it. Raising the bridge lowers the risk, and a ramp helps people who use wheelchairs or push carts. Phone alerts can warn people early, but not everyone has a phone or data. Printed notices at the market reach more people. Making sure that everyone can use a plan is called inclusion. Often, two ideas together work better than one, and it helps to ask the people who use the bridge.

read.sections.0.text.back: The environment is everything around us: land, water, air, plants and animals. The environment changes over time. Because the climate is changing, some places now get heavier rain, while other places have longer dry seasons. People also change places. For example, if many trees are cut down on a hillside, heavy rain can more easily wash the soil away, because there are no longer roots holding it. In Brookside, heavier rain now sometimes covers the low small bridge. Children use the bridge to go to school, and traders use it to go to the market. The community needs a plan.
read.sections.0.text.source: The environment is everything around us: land, water, air, plants and animals. Environments change over time. As the climate changes, some places now get heavier rain, while others have longer dry seasons. People change places too. For example, when many trees are cut down on a hillside, heavy rain can wash the soil away more easily, because there are no roots to hold it. In Brookside, heavier rain now sometimes covers the low footbridge. Children use the bridge to reach school, and traders use it to reach the market. The community needs a plan.

watch.summary.back: In this short UNICEF video, people talk about climate change and disability. Heavy rain, landslides and storms can cause problems for a whole town. But this video says events like these are even harder for children with disabilities. Not all children can hear a warning sound. Not all children can run to a safe place. So these children need a different plan. The main message is to make these plans together, before danger comes. Ask people with disabilities, because they know what they need. The video asks for warnings that are useful for everyone, safe routes for everyone, and safe places everyone can use. If you plan for everyone from the start, the plan is better for all.
watch.summary.source: In this short UNICEF video, people talk about climate change and disability. Heavy rain, landslides and storms can cause problems for a whole town. But the video says these events are even harder for children with disabilities. Not every child can hear a warning sound. Not every child can run to a safe place. So these children need different plans. The main message is to make these plans together, before danger comes. Ask people with disabilities, because they know what they need. The video asks for warnings that work for all, a safe path for all, and safe places that all can use. When you plan for everyone from the start, the plan is better for all.
